messages:
Anna (networking): quick sync: spike showed GWLBE + cross-account role can stitch endpoints into customer VPCs without peering. want a short design call on tradeoffs.
Ben (infra): where do we terminate TLS? app LB in customer VPC or our relay?
Mike (security): prefer customer-side TLS termination so we don't hold certs. downside: we lose client IP unless we use proxy protocol or preserve source IP with specific target types.
Sara (product): customers want source IP for rate-limiting and fraud signals — can we promise it?
Ben (infra): rough options: GWLBE with targets that preserve client ip vs NLB with proxy-protocol. cross-account GWLBE semantics are a bit awkward though.
Anna (networking): spike summary: two viable paths — (a) per-customer ephemeral ENI agent in their account that registers targets locally (preserves src ip), (b) central relay that accepts traffic and SNATs to our fleet (no src ip).
Mike (security): per-customer ENI is stronger isolation but increases IAM surface and operator rotation complexity. we also need KMS auth for any key material.
Ben (infra): also think about scale: ENI warmup and attaching delays will impact bursty traffic. central relay can autoscale faster but has double-hop latency.
Anna (networking): snippet from the spike (sketch):
```
# terraform sketch for customer endpoint
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "gwlbe" {
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-..."
  vpc_id = var.customer_vpc
}
```
Sara (product): what about billing implications? customers will notice data transfer and want clarity in contracts.
Ben (infra): cost note: GWLBE + ENI approach keeps path single-hop (cost ~ standard inter-AZ egress), central relay adds our egress + potential inter-region transfer depending on routing.
Anna (networking): proposal: support both patterns. default = central relay with SNAT for lowest barrier. opt-in = per-customer ENI model (requires role + lightweight agent in customer account). control plane will manage config blobs and rollout policies.
Mike (security): for opt-in path require KMS key policy and explicit role trust. agent should be minimal (lambda or tiny daemon) so customers can audit easily.
Ben (infra): operational requirements: agent must emit health + readiness, we need fast failover to central relay. add TTLs for cache invalidation when switching paths to avoid sticky misroutes.
Anna (networking): RFC TODOs: define interface fields: role_arn, endpoint_config (subnet/route targets), health webhook, failover policy, and terraform/provider examples + migration steps. will draft.
Sara (product): i'll capture customer asks around IP preservation, compliance, and egress billing. will send a prioritized list by EOD. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: created doc stub: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1example-ephemeral-endpoint-stitching (stub)
Ben (infra): small extra: we should propagate a request-id header across boundary for debugging (x-redwood-request-id). helps trace when we handoff between customer-side LB and our relay.
Anna (networking): agreed. add to RFC and include example curl header. ok i'll draft the RFC and ping folks for review tomorrow. thanks all.
